title: Social Media and Videos Linked to Worse Test Scores
paragraphs: Students in Japan who spend more time on social media and watching videos tend to get lower scores on tests, according to new data from Japan's education ministry.

Every year, Japan's education ministry holds a national test for students in the sixth grade of elementary school and the third year of junior high school. In April and May 2026, about 1.84 million students took the test in Japanese and math. Junior high students also took an English test. The students also answered questions about their daily lives.

The survey found that many students spend a lot of time on social media and videos. About 49% of junior high school students said they spend at least three hours on social media or videos on weekdays. This was 17 points higher than in 2024. Among sixth-graders, the figure was about 37%. In addition, 28.5% of junior high students and 21.7% of sixth-graders said they spend at least four hours a day.

The ministry found that students who spent more time on social media and videos had lower scores in all subjects. For example, in math, junior high students who spent at least four hours a day on social media and videos answered 48.7% of the questions correctly. In contrast, those who spent less than 30 minutes answered 69.6% correctly.
Almost all students now have a smartphone or a similar device. Only 4.5% of sixth-graders and 1% of junior high students said they did not have one.
At the same time, students are spending less time studying at home. For example, only about 62% of junior high students said they study for at least one hour on weekdays outside school.
However, the data only show a link between screen time and test scores. They do not prove that screen time causes lower scores.
